messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: encapsulating install in RStan?
parts:
I'd like to try to cut down on the wave of install problems that
are getting reported lately (which may just indicate more users
and may all be Rcpp 0.11.0 related). Here's what I think we can do:

1. *Encapsulate instructions per platform.*

I want to write instructions on a per-platform basis rather
than as a series of steps and instructions like we have now. I
can do that, but Daniel needs to send me the login info for Andrew's
office machine and some hints at how to access its desktop remotely.

2. *Encapsulate our install*

I would like to investigate ways to encapsulate our install
as much as possible. The steps I'd like to take are:

2a. Isolate from user's R config.

Ben mentioned during the meeting that there might be a way to
guarantee that our own Makevars gets used (or if we don't need that,
at least that the system-wide and user-specific one don't get in the
way). What are the steps to do that?

2b. Fix a particular Rcpp version.

Is there a way to use a version of Rcpp other than the most recent
without interfering with the rest of the user's environment? If so,
I'd like to freeze Rcpp versions until we know more recent ones work.

2c. Fix a particular C++ toolchain.

I'd like to have a way to let users pin down a version of the C++ toolchain
that we know works and use that. Is there a way to do that in R?


I wouldn't be averse to letting users try whatever the hell they
want to install easily, but I'd like to have a set of very specific
instructions that are guaranteed to work. I don't care if they're long.
Automateable is better, as Andrew keeps saying.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: encapsulating install in RStan?
parts:
On Saturday, February 15, 2014 10:39:42 AM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:
2a.  Isolate from user's R config.

Ben mentioned during the meeting that there might be a way to
guarantee that our own Makevars gets used (or if we don't need that,
at least that the system-wide and user-specific one don't get in the
way).  What are the steps to do that?

remove.packages("rstan")
Sys.setenv(R_MAKEVARS_USER = "foobar")
Sys.setenv(R_MAKEVARS_SITE = "foobar")
options(repos = c(getOption("repos"), rstan = "http://wiki.rstan-repo.googlecode.com/git/"))
install.packages(c("inline", "Rcpp"))
install.packages('rstan', type = 'source')
Sys.unsetenv("R_MAKEVARS_USER")
Sys.unsetenv("R_MAKEVARS_SITE")
library(rstan)
set_cppo("fast")

2b.  Fix a particular Rcpp version.

Is there a way to use a version of Rcpp other than the most recent
without interfering with the rest of the user's environment?  If so,
I'd like to freeze Rcpp versions until we know more recent ones work.

You can fairly easily require a minimum version of Rcpp or any package. But I don't think you can require a maximum version or a particular version on CRAN. There is

http://rstudio.github.io/packrat/

but that is more for joint development. I don't think it is good form or practice to try to dictate what Rcpp people use. There are like 160 R packages that use Rcpp in some way and it is quite possible that one of them needs functionality in whatever the latest version of Rcpp is. But as long as we are spending money on bodyguards for conferences anyway ...

2c.  Fix a particular C++ toolchain.

I'd like to have a way to let users pin down a version of the C++ toolchain
that we know works and use that.  Is there a way to do that in R?

I don't know of any toolchain that is incapable of working except for the Compiler Suite Formerly Known as Sun Studio, which in fairness didn't work even before it got Oracled.

CRAN itself has started checking packages with clang on !Windows

http://cran.r-project.org/web/checks/check_flavors.html#r-devel-linux-x86_64-debian-clang

But you can't say, "just use clang++" because it is hard to install on Windows. Nor can you say "just use g++" because there really is no such entity. What is symlinked as g++ on Xcode is really llvm-g++-4.2 and what is called g++ on Windows is really mingw and based on g++-4.6. Neither are really supported by what would be considered upstream g++.

So, at a minimum, you are left with saying "just use X on platform Y". But I still think that is a bad idea. You need people to try the software with as many compilers as possible in order to find bugs.

I wouldn't be averse to letting users try whatever the hell they
want to install easily, but I'd like to have a set of very specific
instructions that are guaranteed to work.  I don't care if they're long.
Automateable is better, as Andrew keeps saying.

I think we only have a few systematic problems on stan-users
  1. Stuff like -g on Windows which prevents stanc and some models from compiling
  2. OS / Xcode versions
I almost never have compiler problems. Not that I am representative but it implies that the problems are less with Stan than with the users' environments. And they wouldn't be major problems if we had binary installs.

Ben

I don't want people to try the software with different platforms
and find bugs. I want to recommend configurations that work.
We just don't have the personnel to spend all our time in testing
combinatorics.

As is, Andrew can't even install RStan because of all these issues!
And I don't know enough about all the dependencies to help, and
all the suggestions are trickled out a bit at a time and it's not
clear to me what's compatible with what (for example, use clang++ in
makevars on Mac but then use a dummy makevars, which seem incompatible).

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: encapsulating install in RStan?
parts:
On Sunday, February 16, 2014 11:30:00 AM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:
(Ben --- would you mind helping Andrew fix his install.  I'm
lost in all the suggestions that have gone by.)
I'm not that helpful with Macs, but it would seem that he just needs to agree to the license before trying to do anything involving compilation.

Whether they should or not, I think people would install
our binaries.  I installed WinBUGS and JAGS binaries outside
of CRAN.  At the very least we could get Andrew out of the
hole he's in.   It's not like we couldn't put nasty stuff in
our source, so they shouldn't trust building it themselves
any more.

You can do

R CMD INSTALL --build rstan*

on any platform to build a binary for that platform. We just need some place to put them.

Now, onto specifics.

2a.  Do we somehow then need to add the makevars back in
to deal with the Rcpp issue?

"The" Rcpp issue at the moment (not building with llvm-g++-4.2) is probably going to be short-lived. As far as I understand, that is a problem with compiling models, rather than installing the rstan package. But at the moment, I guess you have to (and want to) specify CXX = clang++ in Makevars before trying to compile a model.

2b.  I was hoping we could fix an Rcpp for Stan, not for
all of R.  I hate hate hate all the dependencies introduced
by the way R (and Linux apparently) manage installs.   We've had no
end of trouble with modified versions of things outside of our
control breaking our builds.

The only thing that I know of that does this is packrat, which I mentioned earlier

http://rstudio.github.io/packrat/

The package management of Debian, which CRAN is based on, is widely considered to be first-rate. I have about 1900 libraries on my laptop. I update them every day or two if new versions are available. It mostly works fine and it gets fixed in a day or two when it is broken.

There may be 160 packages that use Rcpp, but my guess is that
they're breaking all the time because their tests aren't thorough
enough.  Just a guess.  Either that, or we're doing something really
wrong in our use of Rcpp compared to the 160 other packages that
got it right.

They aren't breaking that often because CRAN won't permit a new Rcpp that breaks packages that depends on it. We just aren't covered by that policy because we aren't on CRAN. They thought they had it before the latest release

http://lists.r-forge.r-project.org/pipermail/rcpp-devel/2014-January/007048.html

although the thing with lists and llvm-g++-4.2 slipped through because it wasn't a compiler / OS that they had access to.

2c.  This answers my earlier question about just setting clang++
on Windows.  Grr.  Arg.

Clang++ on Windows is much farther behind than it is on Mac / Linux. It might not be any better than mingw at this point and at a minimum, it depends on the mingw headers currently. However, Stan with the mingw based on g++-4.8 is currently untenable. It takes more than 7.5 GB of memory to do some of the individual tests under src/test/unit/mcmc/hmc on a 64bit OS. We are surviving due to Rtools continuing to bundle a forked prerelease of mingw based on g++-4.6. If they ever bump, then Stan isn't going to be usable on Windows for a lot of people. Maybe by that time, one of the various refactorings will have fixed things or maybe clang++ will be ready.

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: encapsulating install in RStan?
parts:
On Sunday, February 16, 2014 2:11:15 PM UTC-5, Ben Goodrich wrote:
Now, onto specifics.

2a.  Do we somehow then need to add the makevars back in
to deal with the Rcpp issue?

"The" Rcpp issue at the moment (not building with llvm-g++-4.2) is probably going to be short-lived. As far as I understand, that is a problem with compiling models, rather than installing the rstan package. But at the moment, I guess you have to (and want to) specify CXX = clang++ in Makevars before trying to compile a model.

And you can automate that by doing (after set_cppo("fast"))

system("echo 'CC=clang' >> ~/.R/Makevars")
system("echo 'CXX=clang++' >> ~/.R/Makevars")

Ben
